questions.content:
Speaking — Part 1 - Personal information

Can you describe a typical day for you? What do you usually do from morning to evening?
questions.sampleAnswer: On a typical day, I wake up at about six o'clock in the morning. First, I have breakfast with my family, and then I go to work by motorbike. In the evening, I come home, have dinner, and watch TV to relax before I go to bed.

questions.content:
Speaking — Part 1 - Personal information

What was the first school you went to like? What do you remember about it?
questions.sampleAnswer: My first school was a small primary school near my house. It had a big yard with many green trees. I remember my first teacher was very kind and gentle. At first I was a little shy, but I soon made many good friends there.

questions.content:
Speaking — Part 1 - Personal information

Can you tell me about your family? Who are the members and what are they like?
questions.sampleAnswer: There are four people in my family: my parents, my younger brother, and me. My father is a teacher, and my mother works in a hospital. My brother is still a student at high school. We love each other and often spend our weekends together.

questions.content:
Speaking — Part 2 - Describe a picture

Describe the picture.
questions.sampleAnswer: In this picture, I can see a young woman standing on a busy city street. She is looking up at a very tall office building in front of her. The building is a modern skyscraper made of glass and steel, and it has many floors. The woman is wearing smart clothes, like a coat, and she is carrying a bag on her shoulder, so maybe she is going to work. The sky is bright and blue behind the tall building. There are also some other smaller buildings and a few people walking on the street. I think the woman is impressed because the building is so high. It looks like a big, modern city centre.

questions.content:
Speaking — Part 2 - Describe a picture

Tell me about the last time you saw a very tall building.
questions.sampleAnswer: The last time I saw a very tall building was last month in Ho Chi Minh City. It was Landmark 81, the tallest building in Vietnam. I went there with my family on the weekend. We took the lift to a very high floor and looked at the whole city below us. I felt a little scared but also very excited. The view was really beautiful.

questions.content:
Speaking — Part 2 - Describe a picture

Why do you think many people like to work in tall buildings?
questions.sampleAnswer: I think many people like to work in tall buildings for a few reasons. First, tall buildings are usually modern and clean, so the offices are very comfortable. Second, they are often in the city centre, so it is easy to travel to work. Also, the high floors have a beautiful view of the city. Finally, working in a tall building can make people feel proud and professional.

questions.content:
Speaking — Part 3 - Compare two pictures

Compare these two pictures.
questions.sampleAnswer: In the first picture, I can see a man working from home. He is sitting at a desk in his living room and using a laptop. He is wearing casual clothes and looks very relaxed and comfortable. In contrast, the second picture shows a group of people working together in a big office. They are wearing smart clothes and sitting at their desks with computers. The office looks modern and professional. The first picture is about working alone at home, which is quiet and free. But the second picture is about working with colleagues in a company, which is busy and more formal. Both pictures show people working, but the places and the feelings are very different.

questions.content:
Speaking — Part 3 - Compare two pictures

Which place would you prefer to work in, and why?
questions.sampleAnswer: I would prefer to work from home rather than in an office. First, I can save a lot of time because I do not have to travel every day. Second, my home is quiet, so I can focus on my work easily. I can also wear comfortable clothes and make my own schedule. However, sometimes I might feel a little lonely without my colleagues around me.

questions.content:
Speaking — Part 3 - Compare two pictures

Do you think more people will work from home in the future? Why?
questions.sampleAnswer: Yes, I think more people will work from home in the future. Nowadays, the internet is very fast, and there are many useful apps for online meetings. So people can do their jobs from almost anywhere. Working from home also saves time and money for travelling. However, some jobs still need people to be at the office, so not everyone can work from home.

questions.content:
Speaking — Part 4 - Discuss an abstract topic

I'd like you to talk about a time when someone gave you feedback about your work or study. Please say who gave you the feedback, what it was about, and what you did after that.
questions.sampleAnswer:
I'd like to talk about a time when my manager gave me feedback at work. It happened about six months ago, when I was still new at my company. I had written my first report, and I was quite proud of it. My manager read it carefully and then called me into her office. She told me that my ideas were good, but my report was too long and a bit difficult to understand. At first, I was surprised. After that, I asked her how to make it better. She showed me how to use shorter sentences and clear headings. Then I rewrote the report, and it looked much more professional.

When I received that feedback, I felt a little sad and nervous at the beginning. But later, I felt thankful because my manager only wanted to help me improve.

In my opinion, feedback is really important. It helps us see our mistakes and become better at our job. Without feedback, we cannot know what we are doing wrong, so we will never grow.
